metadata.title: EGB-001: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis with Thermo Fisher UltraPure Agarose
metadata.purpose: Analyze PCR products, plasmid digests, or restriction fragments by agarose gel electrophoresis.
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft for casting an UltraPure agarose gel with 1X TAE/TBE-style buffer, DNA ladder, and DNA stain. Confirm the current manufacturer protocol, SDS, and local EHS rules before bench use.
beforeYouBegin: Select agarose percentage based on expected fragment size: higher agarose resolves smaller fragments and lower agarose resolves larger fragments.
Use the same buffer for gel casting and running to avoid distorted migration.
Confirm stain compatibility with downstream cloning; use safer alternatives or blue light when extracting DNA.
Check that the gel is level, wells are intact, and buffer covers the gel by a thin layer.

materials.name: Electrophoresis buffer
materials.specification: Use TAE or TBE-style buffer; use the same buffer for casting and running

equipment.name: Power supply
equipment.settings: Use the selected voltage; confirm electrode orientation before starting

equipment.name: Gel imaging system
equipment.settings: Use correct excitation and emission settings

equipment.name: Blue-light transilluminator
equipment.settings: Optional; use to reduce DNA damage when bands will be excised

tables.title: Run Record Template
tables.note: Blank run-record template provided in the source PDF.

steps.action: Prepare agarose in the selected 1X running buffer and dissolve completely by heating.
Cool molten agarose before adding stain when using in-gel stain.

parameters.rawText: Cool molten agarose to about 50-60 deg C before adding stain if using in-gel stain.

steps.action: Pour gel into the casting tray with comb installed, remove bubbles, and allow the gel to solidify fully.
steps.expectedResult: Level, fully solidified gel with intact wells.

steps.action: Place the gel in the electrophoresis chamber and cover it with 1X running buffer.
Mix DNA samples with loading dye unless already prepared in loading buffer.
Load DNA ladder into at least one lane and load samples carefully without puncturing wells.
Confirm that wells are near the negative electrode so DNA migrates toward the positive electrode.
steps.criticalNotes: Confirm electrode orientation before starting electrophoresis.

steps.action: Run at the selected voltage until the dye front reaches the appropriate distance.
Image the gel using the correct excitation and emission settings.
Save the image file with date, gel ID, ladder, sample map, and exposure settings.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Expected ladder bands should be sharp and in correct order.
Samples should migrate in the expected direction with minimal smiling or lane leakage.

steps.expectedResult: Gel image can be used for size estimation, purity assessment, or band-excision notes.

controls.name: DNA ladder
controls.description: Load into at least one lane; its expected bands should be sharp and in correct order.

expectedOutputs: Saved gel image with gel ID, ladder, sample map, and exposure settings.

troubleshooting.cause: Electrodes reversed, power off, or wrong chamber setup.
troubleshooting.solution: Check leads, voltage, buffer level, and sample loading direction.

troubleshooting.cause: Excess voltage, overheating, or uneven gel.
troubleshooting.solution: Lower voltage, use fresh buffer, and cast the gel level.

troubleshooting.cause: Too much DNA, degraded sample, or wrong agarose percentage.
troubleshooting.solution: Load less DNA, use fresh sample, and adjust gel percentage.

troubleshooting.cause: Low DNA amount, wrong stain/filter, or short exposure.
troubleshooting.solution: Check stain and imager settings; load more DNA or image longer.

safety: Wear a lab coat, gloves, and eye protection; treat gels, stains, UV exposure, and probes according to local EHS rules.
Use a fume hood for powdered stains and hazardous probe or detection reagents when required.
For cloning-grade DNA, minimize UV exposure and document excision band size.
